A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 26 readable pages, including Appendices A–F. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support comparison of the equations, figures, table and appendices without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original numerical verification of counterexamples, smoothed-rectification experiments and DSBM convergence experiments in Appendices D–F, including Table 1 and Figures 3–17.

after.justification: v3 retains the original numerical experiments and outcomes in Appendices D–F, including transport distances, simulated trajectories and marginal-error measurements.

M1.justification: The rectification losses, gradient constraint and smoothed-rectification procedure in Section 5 are unchanged. The added stochastic-interpolant terminology concerns naming and attribution.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic transport setups, including the disconnected-support example from Section 4.1 and the Gaussian-source construction in Remark 12. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains standard rectification at c0=0 alongside the same smoothed variants. The optimal-coupling references and DSBM experiments are also unchanged; expanded citations introduce no evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Appendices D–F retain the same training settings, initial couplings, noise levels, iteration counts and metrics. Appendix F still uses 50 DSBM iterations, regularization values 0.05, 0.1, 0.5 and 1, and 50,000 samples for metric evaluation.

E4.justification: The appendix analyses of fixed points under different initializations, smoothing-noise sensitivity, and DSBM convergence and marginal errors are identical. No robustness test, sensitivity analysis or case study changes.

E5.justification: The numerical studies retain the same reporting practice. Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests, and v3 adds no uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 1 is identical, including step-5 transport distances of 2.79 for c0=0 and 2.66 for c0=0.2. Figures 3–17 and their reported fixed-point, smoothing and DSBM findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, invariance and Gaussian results, counterexamples, rectifiability criterion and smoothing theorem are unchanged. All proofs in Appendices A–C are retained identically; background citation changes concern attribution.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution outline and Section 6 retain the same scientific claims about rectified flows, counterexamples to optimal-transport equivalence and smoothed rectification. Their scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations are retained, including initialization dependence, unresolved convergence to optimal transport, the Gaussian-source restriction for smoothing, and slow DSBM convergence at low regularization.

D1.justification: Implementation information is identical, including Appendix D's three 512-unit hidden layers, 40,000 Adam steps and batch size 256. POT usage and sampling details are unchanged, with no added code, data-access or hardware information.

R1.justification: Sections 1–2.1 broaden attribution to Albergo and Vanden-Eijnden [2] and explicitly name stochastic interpolants. A new sentence connects [1, 2] to flow matching and (entropic) optimal transport through nonlinear interpolants. Both works were already in the bibliography, making this a limited positioning revision.

P1.justification: A few introduction and background passages incorporate stochastic-interpolant terminology and expanded attribution. Page 11 adds a funding acknowledgement for Chambolle. The section structure and remaining prose, including the appendices, are unchanged.

P2.justification: Text reflows across pages 2–3, and the expanded acknowledgement shifts reference spacing on page 11. All 17 figures and Table 1 retain identical content, captions, placement and layout.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the prior-work context more complete through broader stochastic-interpolant attribution and the explicit connection between nonlinear interpolants and (entropic) optimal transport. This provides a modest improvement in scholarly framing. The theory, empirical evidence and limitations, including all appendices, remain unchanged.
